decisions.why: The Latin has no article. The line is said alone as a Lauds antiphon (*Te decet hymnus, * Deus, in Sion*, Psalmi major) and as the Requiem Introit verse, and the Te Deum's close has *te decet hymnus* (Common/Prayers.txt) — the definite article makes it the hymn owed to God, which is what *decet* says. *convém* follows 32:1 *rectos decet collaudátio → aos retos convém louvar*; here the thing befitting is a noun and God is its dative, so the misreading found at 32:1 (praise they deserve) is the right sense here (πρέπει).

options.note: draft — the hymn that is God's due; the antiphon's first half 'A vós convém o hino' stands alone

options.label: um hino
options.note: DM1962 'A Ti convém, ó Deus, em Sião, um hino' — his order and article

options.label: os hinos (MS1932)
options.note: MS1932 'são devidos os hinos' — plural against the Latin singular

decisions.why: *reddere vota → pagar os votos* is the psalter's use so far (21:26, 49:14, 55:12, 60:9). The Latin is a future passive with no agent; *será pago* keeps the voice.

options.label: será pago
options.note: draft — future passive, as the Latin; the verb of 21:26, 49:14, 60:9

options.label: se pagará
options.note: the impersonal reflexive; same sense, lighter

options.label: será cumprido
options.note: how a vow is 'paid' in Portuguese; but it breaks the *pagar* family of 21:26, 49:14, 60:9

decisions.why: *omnis caro* (πᾶσα σάρξ) is the biblical 'all flesh'; MS1932 glosses it away (*todos os mortais*). Rule 5: the concrete word stays. The line is also an Office of the Dead antiphon (*Exáudi, Dómine, * oratiónem meam: ad te omnis caro véniet*, Commune/C9.txt), where 'flesh' coming to God is the point. Order: *a vós virá toda a carne* ends the verse on the noun, as the Latin ends on its verb; the Latin order *a vós toda a carne virá* is the literal tier.

options.label: toda a carne
options.note: draft — the Latin's word, as 55:5 *carne* for *caro*

options.label: todo mortal
options.note: MS1932's sense ('todos os mortais'); explains the image

decisions.why: The glossary row *propitiári → ser propício* (open) names 64:4 among the places it must serve; 24:11 *propitiáberis peccáto meo → sereis propício ao meu pecado* is the same verb in the same tense with a dative of the sin. Kept for that echo, and because *perdoar* is *dimíttere*'s. The row's known cost: one blind reader did not know *propício*. *tu* is emphatic in the Latin, so *vós* is named.

options.label: sereis propício
options.note: draft — the glossary row, as 24:11

options.label: perdoareis
options.note: MS1932 *perdoarás*, DRB *pardon*; clearer, but spends *dimíttere*'s verb

decisions.why: *assúmere* with a person as object → *recolher* (open row; 17:17, 26:10 *o Senhor, porém, me recolheu*), and the row names 64:5 as its third place. προσελάβου is 'take to oneself'. The internal echo *escolhestes / recolhestes* is the Latin's own (*elegísti / assumpsísti*). **v2:** all three readers stopped at *recolhestes* (Latinist: a shift toward sheltering; stylist: a jingle with *escolhestes*, and taking in laundry; blind reader: gathering up). Here God takes a chosen man to himself — the Latinist's *tomastes para vós* says it. The glossary row stays *recolher* for 17:17 and 26:10, where a man is drawn out of danger; 64:5 is noted there as the exception.

options.label: tomastes para vós
options.note: v2 — the Latinist's fix (προσελάβου, take to oneself); the stylist and the blind reader both heard *recolhestes* as gathering things up

options.label: recolhestes
options.note: draft 1 — the glossary row (17:17, 26:10); heard as gathering things / jingle with *escolhestes*

options.label: tomastes
options.note: the bare verb (literal tier)

decisions.why: One Latin verb three times in the psalm (πίμπλημι / πληρόω), so one Portuguese verb. *encher / cheio* follows 25:10 *repléta est munéribus → está cheia de dádivas*. 62:6's *fartar-se* (for the jussive *repleátur*) cannot serve here: 64:12 *replebúntur ubertáte* would say *se fartarão de fartura*. The two futures are passive in the Latin and stay passive (*Seremos cheios … serão cheios*), which also makes them echo; the perfect passive *replétum est* is a state, *está cheio*, as 25:10. MS1932 *Seremos cheios dos bens da tua casa*.

options.label: Seremos cheios / está cheio / serão cheios
options.note: draft — passive, as the Latin; 25:10's word

options.label: pronominal: Encher-nos-emos / encheu-se / se encherão
options.note: MS1932 has *encheu-se de águas* and *se encherão*; the voice changes (the Latinist marked that in adimplére, 16:14b)

options.label: repletos / repleto
options.note: the cognate; bookish

decisions.why: The row *salutáris (of God, in apposition) → Salvador* (open) says *Deus salutáris noster* (64:6) 'will test the line' against D6's neuter *salutáre → salvação*. Here the Greek is ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν — the person, not the thing — so *Salvador*, as 23:5 and 24:5. DRB 'O God our saviour', MS1932 *ó Deus, Salvador nosso*. The possessive before the noun, as 24:5 *o meu Salvador*.

options.label: nossa salvação

decisions.latin: spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe
decisions.why: *et in mari longe* hangs loosely on *spes*: hope of the ends of the earth, and (hope) in the sea far off — those far away on the sea, or the far sea itself. The Latin leaves it open and so does *e no mar ao longe*; DRB 'and in the sea afar off' likewise. MS1932 resolves it (*e das longínquas praias do mar*). The colon is also a Preces response on its own (*R. Spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe*, Special/Preces.txt), so it must stand without the vocative.

options.label: e no mar, ao longe
options.note: v2 — the stylist's comma, so the adverb is heard apart; the relation left open, as the Latin

forms.inmari: e dos que estão longe no mar

options.note: resolves it to the people at sea; +3 syllables

options.label: e do mar distante
options.note: makes the sea a second genitive of *spes*; the adverb becomes an adjective

decisions.why: 64:7 continues the appositions to *Deus* of 64:6: a participle, then *qui* with a second person. A Portuguese gerund at the head of a verse dangles; *Vós que preparais … que perturbais* makes both members relative clauses and names the addressee, which the Latin's second person implies. *preparar* (not MS1932's *Dás firmeza aos montes*, which interprets) because the psalm returns to the root twice in 64:10b (*parásti … præparátio*).

options.label: Vós que preparais … que perturbais
options.note: draft — two relative clauses

options.label: Preparando … vós que perturbais
options.note: the participle kept as a gerund; the subject arrives in the second colon

decisions.why: The glossary's *in virtúte tua → no vosso poder* (20:2, 20:14, 53:3). Here *in* is instrumental (with it he prepares the mountains); *com* would be the natural preposition, but the formula is kept identical, and *no vosso poder* can be heard as 'by means of' too. Note the Latin has *tua* where the Greek has αὐτοῦ; the Latin is followed.

options.label: com o vosso poder
options.note: v2 — the stylist: *no vosso poder* was heard as locative, where the Latin is instrumental; the preposition is grammar (D2)

options.label: no vosso poder

decisions.why: *virtus* (*poder*) and *poténtia* stand in one verse, so they must differ (the *virtus* row says so for 64:7). δυναστεία: lordly might. *força* is *fortitúdo*'s, *vigor* a man's *virtus*. *potência* is the cognate and the plain word for power in Brazil (engine, world power); *poderio* is closer to 'dominion' but rarer. Proposed as a glossary row (open): *poténtia → potência*. *cingido* keeps *accíngere* one verb with 64:13 *accingéntur → serão cingidas*, and with *præcíngere → cingir* (17:33).

options.label: potência
options.note: draft — the cognate, apart from *poder*

options.label: poderio
options.note: 'dominion', closer to δυναστεία; a little literary

options.label: força
options.note: plainest, but it is *fortitúdo*'s word

decisions.why: The glossary keeps *términi (terræ) → limites* apart from *fines terræ → confins* (2:8). The psalm has both two verses apart (64:6 *fínium*, 64:8 *términos*); the Greek is πέρατα in both, so D15's test would allow one word, but the Latin varies and the row exists. Kept apart; *confins* is the option.

options.label: os limites
options.note: draft — the glossary row (2:8)

options.label: nos extremos
options.note: the stylist's proposal: plain and spatial, but a new word for the psalter

decisions.why: *timére a* + ablative → a direct object (the *timére* row). *a signis* could also be 'because of' (MS1932 *pelos teus prodígios*, DRB 'at thy signs'); the plain object keeps the Latin's openness and is shortest in a colon already four syllables over. *sinais*, not *prodígios* (which is *prodígium*'s).

decisions.why: The hardest words of the psalm. The Greek is ἐξόδους πρωίας καὶ ἑσπέρας — 'the goings-out of morning and of evening' (both genitive); the Latin's *véspere* can be read as a second genitive (DRB 'the outgoings of the morning and of the evening') or as 'at evening'. *As saídas* keeps the concrete noun without deciding what they are (sunrise and sunset, the east and the west — MS1932 resolves to *as regiões do oriente e do ocidente*, which is a gloss). The object comes after the verb, the natural Portuguese order. **After the v2 gate:** the ablative reading is taken — the form is the Latin's, and the Latin is what is translated.

options.label: as saídas da manhã, e à tarde

forms.exitus: as saídas da manhã, e à tarde

decisions.why: Active, causative *delectáre*: at 29:2 (*nec delectásti inimícos meos*) it went to *alegrar*. The Greek differs (τέρψεις here, εὐφραίνω there), but the Latin verb and voice are the same, so the same verb. *deleitar* is the deponent *delectári*'s (50:18, 36:4).

options.note: draft — as 29:2

options.label: deleitareis

decisions.why: The *inebriáre → embriagar* row (open) names both places. The image — the earth made drunk with rain — is the Latin's and the Greek's (ἐμέθυσας, μέθυσον); MS1932 glosses it (*inebriaste (com chuvas benéficas)*). Kept, one verb for both, as the Latin.

decisions.why: A Hebraism through the Greek (ἐπλήθυνας τοῦ πλουτίσαι αὐτήν): 'you multiplied to enrich it' = you enriched it abundantly. Portuguese cannot take *multiplicar* + infinitive. The draft keeps the verb *multiplicar* (which returns in 64:11 *multíplica*) and turns the infinitive into its noun, *riqueza*; *sua* can only be the earth's, since God is *vossa*. DRB 'thou hast many ways enriched it' keeps the enriching and makes the multiplying an adverb — option.

options.label: multiplicastes a sua riqueza
options.note: draft — *multiplicar* kept; the infinitive becomes a noun

options.label: de muitos modos a enriquecestes
options.note: DRB; 62:2b already renders *multiplíciter* 'de quantos modos'

options.label: multiplicastes para a enriquecer
options.note: the Latin's build; the verb has no object

options.label: multiplicastes o enriquecê-la
options.note: the Latinist's minor (v1): keeps the infinitive and *eam*; a nominalised infinitive with an enclitic is not said in Portuguese

decisions.why: *rivus* is a stream (the Greek αὔλακας, 'furrows', is not followed — rule 1). The plainest Brazilian word.

decisions.why: *genímina* (γενήματα) is what the earth brings forth. *frutos* is *fructus*'s word (a different Greek, καρπός); *colheitas* names the produce of the land plainly. MS1932 *as suas produções*.

decisions.why: *gérminans* is a participle: either predicative with an unexpressed subject (the earth will rejoice, sprouting — the Greek has ἀνατέλλουσα, feminine, the earth) or substantive ('the sprouting thing will rejoice'). The gerund keeps the Latin's build and leaves the subject unnamed, as the Latin does. *com as suas gotas*: *in* + ablative taken as the means; *nas suas gotas* is not idiomatic Portuguese.

options.label: o que germina
options.note: v2 — the Latinist and the stylist both read *gérminans* as the subject; the blind reader heard no subject in the gerund. *germina* is paroxytone (ger-MI-na), so the cadence holds

options.note: draft 1 — the participle as a gerund; subject left unnamed

options.label: o que brota

decisions.why: πιανθήσονται, 'grow fat' — the *pinguis → gordo* family. Fat land is fertile land (*terra gorda* is still said), so the image is kept (rule 5) rather than explained as MS1932 does (*ficarão viçosas*). **v2:** the stylist called it the worst line (comic) and the blind reader was confused; with *os lugares formosos* the subject is now plainly land, which is where *engordar* has its farming sense. Kept (rule 5: fat stays fat); *Ficarão fartos* is the option.

The cost: *beleza* is already *spécies*' word at 46:5 (and *pulchritúdo*'s at 44:5a) — same root family as *speciósa*, so a reader crossing columns loses little.

choices.64:2: The Lauds antiphon divides after *hymnus* (*Te decet hymnus, * Deus, in Sion*): *A vós convém o hino, * Deus, em Sião* divides the same way. Bare vocative *Deus*, as the finished psalms. The blind reader half-heard *voto* as a ballot; *pagar os votos* is the psalter's established phrase (21:26, 49:14, 60:9), kept.
choices.64:4: *super nos → sobre nós* (the Latin's preposition; 12:4b's *contra* is *advérsus*). *impíetas → impiedade*, as 5:11b and 31:5b. *vós sereis propício às nossas impiedades* puts the verb before its dative so the verse ends on a paroxytone. **The blind reader heard *propício às nossas impiedades* as God favouring our sins** — the second reader to hear the row's adjective that way (24:11). Kept for the row; the main session should look at *propitiári* before 77:38, 78:9.
choices.64:5: *aquele que* rather than MS1932's *o que*, which a Brazilian ear can take as 'what'. *inhabitáre → habitar*. *átrio* kept (the row), though the blind reader did not know it (the third). The first colon is +8 against the Latin in v2 (*Bem-aventurado*, D19, and *tomastes para vós*); one breath still.
choices.64:5b: *os bens da vossa casa* as 26:13 *os bens do Senhor*. *mirábilis → maravilhoso* (row), *æquitas → equidade* (36:37a, 51:5).
choices.64:7: *profúndum maris → o fundo do mar* (67:23 has the same phrase). *sonum* is in apposition to *profúndum*, and stays so: *o fundo do mar, o som das suas ondas* (MS1932 adds a verb in a gloss). *sonus → som*, as 18:5. *conturbáre → perturbar* (row).
choices.64:8: *Turbabúntur gentes → As nações se perturbarão*: *turbáre → perturbar*, the middle as 47:6 *perturbaram-se*. The first colon runs long (+3 against the Latin in v2) because Portuguese needs *os que* for *qui*; it is one breath. *éxitus … véspere*: the blind reader found *as saídas da manhã* opaque (exits, departures). It is the Latin's own crux, left concrete and unresolved on purpose (decision `exitus`).
choices.64:10b: *parásti … præparátio* and 64:7 *Prǽparans*: one root, *preparar … preparação*, as the Latin. *ejus* (the Greek has σου) → *a sua*, whose antecedent is left as open as the Latin's. *cibus → alimento*. *illórum → deles*, to keep it off the river. First colon +5 (accepted: *preparastes-lhes o alimento* would save one syllable but *lhes* lands on the river's *águas*; *o seu alimento* could be the river's). The blind reader found *deles* without antecedent and *a sua preparação* opaque; the Latin's *illórum* and *ejus* are just as unanchored (and the Greek has σου), so neither is resolved.
choices.64:12: *Benedíces → Bendireis* (the *benedícere* row), *corónæ → a coroa* (the crown kept, as the *coronáre* row), *benignitátis → benignidade* (D44 names this verse), *ubertáte → fartura* (the *ubértas* row names this verse).
choices.64:13: *accingéntur → serão cingidas*, passive as the Latin, echoing 64:7 *cingido*. *colles → colinas*. *exsultátio → exultação* (row; unknown to the blind reader again). First colon +4 in v2.
choices.64:6: Second colon +5: *esperança de todos os confins da terra* alone matches the Latin's words one for one; the rest is *in mari longe*, kept whole (decision `inmari`). The colon also stands alone as a Preces response.

audit.note: Draft 1 from the parallels (Latin, LXX, DRB, MS1932, DM1962 for diction). Hard readings: 64:8 *éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis* (the Greek's two genitives followed, left concrete); 64:10 *multiplicásti locupletáre eam* (Hebraism — the verb kept, the infinitive made a noun); 64:11 *gérminans* (gerund, subject open); 64:7 *virtus* and *poténtia* in one verse (*poder* / *potência*). Glossary rows applied: exaudíre, propitiári, assúmere, salutáris, in virtúte tua, inebriáre, benígnitas, ubértas, aríes, timére a, términi, delectáre (29:2), psalmum dícere. The psalm's own repetitions kept: *replére* ×3, *inebriáre* ×2, *multiplicáre* ×2, *(præ)paráre* ×3, *accíngere* ×2, *hymnus* ×2.
